propositions: Ubuntu jobs occupy 30.2 runner-minutes per Verified run (py3.11=615s, py3.12=634s, py3.13=563s) across default and integration phases, blocking org-wide runner capacity.

Bridge cadence test reads and parses the same workflow YAML 1,440 times inside a minute-comprehension loop, costing 7.9s per run; hoisting the parse outside reduces cost to ~0.001s without changing the exhaustive proof.

Pandoc corpus tests invoke the real binary 3,421 times across two suites (test_wiki_render_corpus.py and test_wiki_render_hardening.py) with 884 total eligible units, but hardening uses only a legacy comparator that could be replaced with static expected outputs while keeping product _convert live.

AST provenance fixture setup costs 46–49s per Ubuntu cell by recomputing caller/parent relationships on every invocation; building indices once per process preserves the exact 24 tuples and assertions.

Gerrit Verify jobs with always() predicates on superseded patchsets do not receive GitHub cancellation signals, causing 25m13s admission delays and wasted runner occupancy until the stale run completes naturally.

Moving full Pandoc corpus real-execution replay from per-change Verify to a weekly External Integration workflow preserves all conversion assertions and boundary coverage while freeing 38–184s per Verified run.
